added.claim: The RUNNING shutdown sequence handles only Exception: a java.lang.Error from an onStop callback (LifecycleCallback.handle declares Exception, so NoClassDefFoundError/AssertionError/StackOverflowError escape) or from a shutdown participant (only RuntimeException is caught) leaves runShutdownSequence early. It then skips the owned-resource close, the logger flush and close, and adapter.release; only the finally moves the app to TERMINATED. Owned DB handles stay open, queued RotatingFileLogger records are lost (its writer is a daemon thread), and on the 'naruserve-shutdown' thread the Error ends as an uncaught exception. The failed-start path catches Throwable and still runs every cleanup step, so the two paths into TERMINATED disagree. Later waves add BEFORE_WAIT/AFTER_ON_STOP participants (WebSocket close, temp files) that run on this same path.

Do the same in ShutdownParticipants.run. Add a test where onStop throws AssertionError and the owned resource and logger still close.

added.claim: app.md says shutdown blocks the caller for at most the timeout. The code applies the deadline only to adapter.stop (FR-APP-011 AC-2). onStop callbacks, owned-resource closes and the logger flush (RotatingFileLogger.flush waits until the queue is written) run with no bound after that, so an Android caller that relies on the doc can block longer than the timeout.
